chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Ma'bad, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abdullah al-Wasiti, from Durust ibn Abu Mansur, from Abu Khalid al-Qammat, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: 'The supplication quickest to succeed for the Answering is the supplication of a brother for his brother in his absence. He begins by supplicating for his brother, so the Angel allocated to him says, "Ameen, and for you is the like of it."'

key_terms.بِظَهْرِ الْغَيْبِ: In his absence / behind his back

ai.seo_question: What is the most effective type of supplication for quick acceptance?
ai.summary: Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) emphasizes the efficacy of du'a made behind the back (bi-zahri al-ghayb), noting that the Angel assigned to the supplicant responds with 'Ameen' and grants a similar reward, thereby highlighting the spiritual interconnectedness of the believers. This tradition underscores the concept of mutual spiritual support in Shia ethics, where the unseen presence of angels amplifies the acceptance of prayers offered for one's brethren.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Ma’bad, from Ubeydullah Bin Abdullah Al Wasity, from Dorost Bin Abu Mansour, from Abu Khalid Al Qammat who said,

‘Abu Ja’farasws said: ‘The supplication quickest to succeed for the Answering is a supplication of the brother for his brother in his absence. He begins by the supplication for his brother, so the Angel who is Allocated with him is saying, ‘Ameen, and for you is the like of it’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Ma’Bad from ‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Abd Allah al-Wasity from Durst ibn abu Mansur from abu Khalid al- Qammat who has said the following:

“Abu Ja’far (a.s.) has said, ‘The prayer quickest to success and acceptance is one’s prayer for his brother (in belief) in his absence where one starts praying for him and the angels guarding say, ‘Amin’ You will have twice as much you asked for him.’”
